messages:
matt: Quick proposal: run an "entropy-aware" precision probe. Use token-level surprisal to decide when to keep fp8 vs drop to int8/4bit. aim: cut token-cost on low-surprisal stretches without hurting factuality. thoughts? cc @olivia @raj

olivia: sounds promising. how do you compute surprisal cheaply? we need something that doesn't add much overhead to the critical path.

matt: use the next-token logprob from a tiny cached pruner model (distil-ish) run in shadow. compute rolling mean over last 32 tokens. if mean_logprob > threshold => low surprisal -> allow lower precision. keep fp8 for high surprisal.

raj: two practical concerns: 1) extra model call latency and cost for the pruner, 2) KV cache compatibility if precision switches mid-conv. we need deterministic rules for cache namespace.

sophia: for (1) we can run the pruner asynchronously and only apply decisions in the next chunk. it doesn't block token emission for the current chunk. for (2) runtime must not mutate existing cached keys. if a precision variant would change serialization we either keep both namespaces or defer switching until conv restart.

matt: exact runtime flow sketch: request arrives -> if `X-Precision-Experiment: entropy-probe` header present and conv has no kv-state, sample decision path: run pruner shadow or use cached surprisal -> choose variant for upcoming chunk -> record `precision.variant`, `surprisal.mean`, `sample.id` in trace. fallback: if deg_delta>0.10 (shadow) or latency.p95>200ms -> revert for that conv.

olivia: telemetry: collect `surprisal.mean`, `precision.variant`, `deg_shadow`, `deg_live`, `kv_state_present`, `batch_size`, `seq_len`, `latency.*`, `tokens`. also store a small set of request+response pairs for manual audits.

raj: we should ensure determinism across restarts: seed = hash(conv_id || start_ts) for sampling and store chosen variant in conv metadata. if runtime can't persist, then don't sample for resumed convs.

sophia: UX/API: add optional request field `precision_strategy: {"entropy": {"threshold":0.85, "window":32}}` or simple header for quick canary. prefer header for fast ops rollouts.

matt: safety nets: 1) shadow fp8 baseline for 3% of sampled tokens 2) automatic kill if mean deg_shadow>0.07 over 10k samples 3) manual kill via feature flag. add an incident playbook.

olivia: add a heuristic to avoid 4bit when batch_size<6 or seq_len<20; we saw p95 regressions on small batches previously. also skip sampling for endpoints in enterprise tier unless explicitly opted-in.

raj: note: per-token switching could complicate cache eviction heuristics. add a cache-compat matrix in runtime: if variant A and B incompatible -> runtime keeps separate namespaces and increases memory for sampled convs. we need cost accounting for that.

ci-bot: ci: scheduled canary (eng-ml-entprobe) will run at 09:30 UTC. monitors: surprisal.mean distribution, precision.variant ratio, deg_shadow mean, latency.p95.

sophia: action items: @raj draft cache-compat appendix + cost estimate, @olivia add telemetry fields and alert thresholds, @matt add pruner perf numbers and pseudocode to RFC followup. ci-bot: hold prod deploy until QA signoff.

matt: i'll run synthetic dialogs with abrupt topic shifts to stress-test surprisal gating and post results. thanks!
